coalition_name: Alabama Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person intentionally and repeatedly follows or harasses another person and makes a threat, expressed or implied, with intent to place the victim in reasonable fear of death or serious bodily injury.
criminal_penalty: First degree: Class C felony, 1 year and 1 day to 10 years; second degree (Ala. Code § 13A-6-90.1): Class B misdemeanor, up to 6 months; aggravated first degree: Class B felony, 2 to 20 years
cyber_note: Electronic stalking in the second degree covers placing an electronic tracking device on another person's property without consent or other lawful authorization.
order_duration: Permanent unless the court specifies otherwise or a later order modifies it
order_free_note: No filing fees, service fees, or subpoena costs in Protection from Abuse cases.
order_gap_note: The PFA order is only for a family/household member or current/former sexual/intimate partner — stalking is qualifying 'abuse' under Ala. Code § 30-5-2, but a stranger/neighbor/coworker stalker cannot get a PFA; remedy is criminal prosecution or a general civil injunction. No standalone non-family stalking order statute verified from an official source.
order_name: Protection Order under the Protection from Abuse Act
order_where: Circuit Court in the county where you live, where the defendant lives, where the abuse occurred, or where you are temporarily located to avoid abuse

coalition_name: Alaska Network on Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: A person knowingly engages in a course of conduct that recklessly places another person in fear of death or physical injury, or in fear of the death or physical injury of a family member.
criminal_penalty: Second degree: Class A misdemeanor, up to 1 year; first degree (with an aggravating factor such as violating a protective order, a victim under 16, or a deadly weapon): Class C felony, up to 5 years
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute found; AS 11.41.270 expressly includes electronic communications, GPS monitoring, and installing a device or software to observe or record a person as nonconsensual contact.
order_duration: 6 months unless earlier dissolved by the court
order_free_note: Filing fees may not be charged in any action seeking only the relief provided in AS 18.65.850-18.65.870.
order_name: Protective Order for Stalking and Sexual Assault
order_where: District or superior court; a parent or guardian may file on behalf of a minor

coalition_name: Arizona Coalition to End Sexual and Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person intentionally or knowingly engages in a course of conduct directed toward another person that causes the victim to suffer emotional distress or reasonably fear physical injury, property damage, or death.
criminal_penalty: Class 5 felony (emotional distress or fear of injury), 6 months to 2.5 years; Class 3 felony if the victim reasonably fears death, 2 to 8.75 years
cyber_note: Covers using an electronic communication to terrify, intimidate, threaten, or harass another person; stalking by electronic means is also charged under A.R.S. § 13-2923.
order_duration: 1 year after service on the defendant
order_free_note: A fee shall not be charged for filing a petition under this section.
order_where: Any magistrate, justice of the peace, or superior court judge in Arizona; any court in the state may issue or enforce it

coalition_name: Arkansas Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person knowingly engages in a course of conduct that would place a reasonable person in the victim's position under emotional distress and in fear for his or her safety or a third person's safety.
criminal_penalty: First degree: Class C felony; second degree: Class D felony; third degree: Class A misdemeanor
cyber_note: Harassing communications covers using a telephone, mail, email, text message, social media, or any other electronic communication with the purpose of harassing, annoying, or alarming someone.
order_duration: 90 days to 10 years, at the court's discretion, and renewable
order_gap_note: The Order of Protection under the Domestic Abuse Act requires a family/household/dating relationship; no verified standalone non-family stalking protective order in Arkansas. A 2026 account confirms a judge could not issue one without that relationship.
order_name: Order of Protection under the Domestic Abuse Act of 1991
order_where: Circuit court; file with the circuit clerk in the county where the petitioner resides, where the alleged abuse occurred, or where the respondent may be served

coalition_name: California Partnership to End Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly follows or harasses another person and makes a credible threat with the intent to place that person in reasonable fear for his or her safety or the safety of his or her immediate family.
criminal_penalty: Wobbler: misdemeanor up to 1 year in county jail and/or a $1,000 fine; felony 2, 3, or 4 years in state prison if committed while a restraining order is in effect
cyber_note: Covers electronically distributing, publishing, or emailing another person's personal identifying information or a harassing message to incite unwanted physical contact, injury, or harassment by a third party; Penal Code § 646.9 also expressly includes threats made through an electronic communication device.
order_duration: Up to 5 years, renewable for another 5 years; defaults to 3 years if no expiration date is stated
order_free_note: No fee if the petition involves stalking, violence, or threats of violence; otherwise a filing fee applies.
order_where: Superior Court in the county where you live

coalition_name: Violence Free Colorado
criminal_definition: A person knowingly makes a credible threat and repeatedly follows, approaches, contacts, or places under surveillance another person, or repeatedly engages in conduct that would cause a reasonable person to suffer serious emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: First offense: Class 5 felony, 1 to 3 years (extraordinary risk, up to 4 years) and $1,000 to $100,000 fine; second offense within 7 years or while a protection order is in effect: Class 4 felony
cyber_note: Kiana Arellano's Law covers initiating electronic communication to harass or threaten bodily injury or property damage, or to make an obscene comment; repeated electronic conduct causing serious emotional distress can be charged as stalking under § 18-3-602.
order_duration: Temporary order until a hearing within 14 days; if granted, a permanent civil protection order
order_free_note: No filing fee may be assessed against a petitioner seeking protection as a victim of stalking, and no service fee may be assessed by a state or public agency.
order_where: Municipal court of record, county court, or district court in any county where the acts occurred, where a party resides, or where a party is employed

coalition_name: Connecticut Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person knowingly engages in a course of conduct of two or more acts directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for his or her physical safety or the physical safety of a third person.
criminal_penalty: Second degree: Class A misdemeanor, up to 1 year and $2,000; first degree (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 53a-181c): Class D felony, 1 to 5 years and up to $5,000
cyber_note: Electronic stalking covers using electronic means to cause substantial emotional distress or reasonable fear of serious or fatal injury to the victim, a family member, or an intimate partner.
order_duration: Up to 1 year, extendable by the court on the applicant's motion
order_name: Civil Protection Order for a victim of sexual abuse, sexual assault, or stalking
order_where: Superior Court

coalition_name: Delaware Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person knowingly engages in a course of conduct of 3 or more separate incidents directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear physical injury to himself or herself or another person, or to suffer other significant mental anguish or distress.
criminal_penalty: Class G felony, up to 2 years; Class F felony if an aggravating factor applies; Class C felony if the person possesses a deadly weapon or causes serious physical injury, up to 15 years
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute found; harassment under 11 Del. C. § 1311 covers communicating by telephone, mail, or any other form of written or electronic communication in a manner likely to cause annoyance or alarm.
order_duration: Up to 3 years, renewable for up to 3 years
order_gap_note: The Sexual Violence Protective Order requires non-consensual sexual contact/penetration — stalking alone does not qualify. Stalking victims without a family/dating relationship would use a PFA only if they qualify, otherwise criminal prosecution.
order_where: Superior Court in the county where the petitioner resides, the respondent resides, or the alleged non-consensual sexual conduct occurred

coalition_name: Florida Partnership to End Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly follows, harasses, or cyberstalks another person, or makes a credible threat with the intent to place that person in reasonable fear for his or her safety.
criminal_penalty: Stalking or cyberstalking: first-degree misdemeanor, up to 1 year and $1,000; aggravated stalking: third-degree felony, up to 5 years
cyber_note: Cyberstalking is defined in the same statute as engaging in a pattern of electronic communication directed at a specific person that causes substantial emotional distress and serves no legitimate purpose.
order_duration: Final injunction remains in effect until modified or dissolved, with no automatic expiration date; temporary injunction up to 15 days
order_free_note: The clerk of court may not assess a filing fee for a petition for protection against stalking, and no bond is required.
order_where: Circuit court where the petitioner currently or temporarily resides, where the respondent resides, or where the stalking occurred

coalition_name: Georgia Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person follows, places under surveillance, or contacts another person at or about a place or places without the consent of the other person for the purpose of harassing and intimidating the other person.
criminal_penalty: First offense: misdemeanor, up to 12 months and $1,000; second or subsequent offense: felony, 1 to 10 years; aggravated stalking (O.C.G.A. § 16-5-91): felony, up to 10 years
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute found; O.C.G.A. § 16-5-90 covers broadcasting or publishing, including by electronic publication, a victim's picture, name, address, or phone number in violation of a court order.
order_duration: Temporary orders typically 6 to 12 months; the court may extend the order or convert it to a permanent order
order_free_note: There is no cost to file a petition for a protective order under Georgia's Family Violence Act.
order_where: Superior Court; file with the Clerk of Superior Court in the county where the respondent resides, or where the petitioner lives or the stalking occurred if the respondent lives outside Georgia

coalition_name: Hawaii State Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person commits harassment by stalking by engaging in a course of conduct involving pursuit, surveillance, or nonconsensual contact on more than one occasion without legitimate purpose, with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm or in reckless disregard of that risk.
criminal_penalty: Misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail and a fine up to $2,000; a repeat offense within 5 years is aggravated harassment by stalking under HRS 711-1106.4, a Class C felony.
cyber_note: Hawaii has no separate cyberstalking statute; nonconsensual contact under HRS 711-1106.5 expressly includes contact by telephone, facsimile, or any form of electronic communication, including email.
order_duration: A temporary restraining order lasts up to 90 days; a final injunction lasts up to 3 years.
order_free_note: There is a $15 filing fee, which can be waived in exceptional circumstances.
order_name: Injunction Against Harassment (with Temporary Restraining Order)
order_where: File a written petition in the District Court of the district where you live, where the respondent lives, or where the harassment occurred.

coalition_name: Idaho Coalition Against Sexual & Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Knowingly and maliciously engaging in a course of conduct of repeated nonconsensual contact that would cause a reasonable person substantial emotional distress or fear of death or injury to that person or a family or household member.
criminal_penalty: Second-degree stalking is a misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail and a $1,000 fine; first-degree stalking is a felony, 1 to 5 years in prison and a fine up to $10,000.
cyber_note: Covers using telecommunication, email, text, or other electronic communication with intent to annoy, terrify, threaten, intimidate, harass, or offend, including repeated communications that disturb the peace.
order_duration: Up to 1 year, renewable on motion for good cause.
order_where: File a verified petition with the magistrate division of the district court in the county where the respondent lives, where you live, or where you are temporarily residing.

coalition_name: Illinois Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Knowingly engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person, knowing or having reason to know it would cause a reasonable person to fear for safety or suffer emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: Class 4 felony, 1 to 3 years in prison; a second or subsequent conviction is a Class 3 felony, 2 to 5 years in prison.
cyber_note: Covers harassing another person through electronic communication on at least two occasions, including transmitting threats or creating a harassing website or webpage.
order_duration: An emergency order lasts 14 to 21 days; a plenary order lasts up to 2 years and can be extended.
order_free_note: No fee is charged by the clerk for filing petitions or modifying or certifying orders, and the sheriff serves the papers at no cost to the petitioner (740 ILCS 21/20).
order_where: File a petition in any Illinois circuit court, including the county where either party lives or where the stalking occurred.

coalition_name: Indiana Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Knowingly or intentionally engaging in a course of conduct involving repeated or continuing harassment that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, or threatened, and that actually causes the victim to feel that way.
criminal_penalty: Level 6 felony, 6 months to 2 1/2 years in prison and a fine up to $10,000; a Level 5 felony, 1 to 6 years in prison, if aggravating factors apply.
cyber_note: Indiana has no separate cyberstalking statute; its harassment law covers using a computer network or other electronic communication to communicate with a person or send obscene or profane messages, with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm and no intent of legitimate communication.
order_duration: Normally 2 years, unless the judge sets a different date.
order_free_note: No fees are charged for filing, service of process, witness fees, or subpoena fees in a protection-order case.
order_where: File a petition with the clerk of the court in your county; Indiana also offers online filing through the state Protection Order Registry.

coalition_name: Iowa Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Purposefully engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, or threatened, or to fear bodily injury or death to that person or an immediate family member.
criminal_penalty: A first offense is an aggravated misdemeanor; a second offense is a Class D felony; a Class C felony if committed while subject to a protective order, while using a technological device, or under other aggravating circumstances.
cyber_note: Iowa has no separate cyberstalking statute; stalking under section 708.11 includes repeatedly using a technological device to locate, listen to, or watch a person without authorization or legitimate purpose, which elevates the offense to a Class C felony.
order_duration: A Chapter 236 protective order lasts for a fixed period of up to 1 year, with unlimited extensions if the defendant still poses a threat.
order_free_note: The filing fee and court costs for a Chapter 236 order for protection are waived for the plaintiff, and service is performed without charge to the plaintiff.
order_gap_note: Iowa has no standalone civil stalking order — a stalking victim uses a Chapter 236 Domestic Abuse Protective Order only if the stalker is a family/household member; otherwise protection comes through a criminal No Contact Order under Chapter 664A, issued by the court in a criminal case (not filed by the victim).
order_name: Domestic Abuse Protective Order; criminal No Contact Order
order_where: File a verified petition for a Chapter 236 protective order in the district court of the county where either party lives; a Chapter 664A no-contact order is issued by the court in a criminal case and is not filed by the victim.

coalition_name: Kansas Coalition Against Sexual and Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Recklessly or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct targeted at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for the safety of that person or an immediate family member, and that actually places the targeted person in such fear.
criminal_penalty: A first offense under subsection (a)(1) is a Class A person misdemeanor; a second or subsequent conviction is a severity level 7 person felony, with higher felony levels for protective-order violations and other aggravating circumstances.
cyber_note: Kansas has no separate cyberstalking statute; the stalking statute covers a course of conduct including use of an electronic tracking system to determine the targeted person's location, movement, or travel patterns.
order_duration: A final order lasts for a fixed period of not less than 1 year and not more than 2 years, extendable for 1 to 3 more years, or up to the defendant's lifetime if the order was violated or other statutory conditions are met.
order_free_note: No docket fee is charged for filing a petition under K.S.A. 60-31a04.
order_name: Protection from Stalking, Sexual Assault, or Human Trafficking Order
order_where: File a petition in any Kansas district court.

coalition_name: ZeroV (formerly Kentucky Coalition Against Domestic Violence)
criminal_definition: Intentionally engaging in a course of conduct directed at another person that seriously alarms, annoys, intimidates, or harasses that person, serves no legitimate purpose, and causes substantial mental distress, while consciously disregarding a substantial and unjustifiable risk of causing that distress.
criminal_penalty: Stalking is a Class D felony, 1 to 5 years in prison; it is a Class C felony if a protective order was in effect, a criminal complaint was pending, there was a prior conviction against the same victim within 5 years, a deadly weapon was used, or the acts placed the victim in reasonable fear of sexual contact, physical injury, or death.
cyber_note: Kentucky has no separate cyberstalking statute; the course of conduct in KRS 508.130 expressly includes conduct by computer, the internet, social media, email, text, and other electronic means.
order_duration: A final interpersonal protective order lasts for a period fixed by the court, up to 3 years, and may be reissued for further periods of up to 3 years each.
order_free_note: No filing fee is charged to petition for a protective order in Kentucky.
order_where: File a petition with the Office of Circuit Court Clerk in the county where you live or the county you fled to for safety, for hearing in Circuit (Family) Court.

coalition_name: Louisiana Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Intentionally and repeatedly following or harassing another person in a way that would cause a reasonable person to feel alarmed or to suffer emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: First conviction: a fine of $500 to $1,000 and 30 days to 1 year in jail; penalties increase for later convictions, victims under 18, use of a dangerous weapon, and protective-order violations.
cyber_note: Covers using electronic communication to threaten physical harm or extort, and repeatedly emailing or electronically communicating to threaten, terrify, or harass a person.
order_duration: A final protective order lasts for a fixed period of up to 18 months, extendable after a hearing; the portion ordering the defendant not to abuse, harass, or interfere with the victim may be made indefinite.
order_free_note: Louisiana law prohibits charging a victim for filing, issuing, or serving a protective order for domestic abuse, dating violence, stalking, or sexual assault.
order_name: Order of Protection under the Protection from Stalking Act
order_where: File a petition in any Louisiana district court empowered to hear civil matters, in the parish where you live.

coalition_name: Maine Coalition to End Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Intentionally or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to suffer serious inconvenience or emotional distress, or to fear bodily injury or death to that person, a close relation, or a pet.
criminal_penalty: Stalking is a Class D crime, up to 364 days in jail and a fine up to $2,000; it is a Class C crime, up to 5 years in prison and a $5,000 fine, for repeat offenders and other aggravating circumstances.
cyber_note: Maine has no separate cyberstalking statute; the course of conduct in 17-A M.R.S. § 210-A includes following, monitoring, tracking, observing, surveilling, threatening, or communicating with a person by any action, method, device, or means, including online.
order_duration: An initial final Protection from Harassment order lasts up to 1 year and may be extended.
order_free_note: There is no filing fee if the complaint is related to stalking, domestic violence, sexual assault, sex trafficking, or unlawful dissemination of private images; other harassment complaints may carry a fee.
order_where: File a complaint in the District Court of the division where you or the defendant lives.

coalition_name: Maryland Network Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Engaging in a malicious course of conduct that includes approaching or pursuing another person, with intent to place that person in reasonable fear of serious bodily injury, assault, rape or a sexual offense, false imprisonment, or death, or knowing or reasonably knowing the conduct would cause such fear.
criminal_penalty: Stalking is a misdemeanor, up to 5 years in prison and a fine up to $5,000.
cyber_note: Covers maliciously engaging in a course of conduct through electronic communication that alarms or seriously annoys another, with intent to harass, alarm, or annoy, after a warning to stop and without legal purpose.
order_duration: A final peace order lasts for the period stated in the order, up to 6 months, and may be extended for up to another 6 months after a hearing for good cause.
order_free_note: There is a $46 filing fee and a $40 service fee; the court may waive the filing fee for indigent petitioners but cannot waive the service fee.
order_where: File a petition in the District Court of Maryland in the county where you live; if the court is closed, a District Court commissioner can issue an interim order.

coalition_name: Jane Doe Inc., The Massachusetts Coalition Against Sexual Assault and Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person commits stalking by willfully and maliciously engaging in a knowing pattern of conduct directed at a specific person that seriously alarms or annoys them and would cause a reasonable person substantial emotional distress, plus making a threat intended to place them in imminent fear of death or bodily injury.
criminal_penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison or a fine of up to $1,000, or up to 2 1/2 years in a house of correction, or both.
cyber_note: Criminal harassment under § 43A covers a pattern of conduct by mail or by telephonic, telecommunication, or electronic communication device, including email and internet communications.
order_duration: Up to 1 year
order_free_note: No filing fee shall be charged for the complaint (ch. 258E, § 3(c)).
order_where: District Court, Boston Municipal Court, Superior Court, or Juvenile Court in the county where the plaintiff resides

coalition_name: Michigan Coalition to End Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is a willful course of conduct involving repeated or continuing harassment that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, threatened, harassed, or molested and that actually causes the victim to feel that way.
criminal_penalty: Stalking: misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail or a fine of up to $1,000, or both; aggravated stalking: felony, up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to $10,000, or both (up to 10 years and $15,000 if the victim is under 18 and the offender is at least 5 years older).
cyber_note: Cyberstalking is posting a message through any electronic medium without the victim's consent, knowing it could cause two or more acts of unconsented contact, with intent to terrorize, frighten, or harass the victim.
order_duration: Ex parte PPO: at least 182 days; the judge may set a longer period.
order_free_note: There is no filing fee for a PPO petition in Michigan.
order_name: Personal Protection Order (Nondomestic) — Nondomestic Stalking PPO
order_where: Family division of the circuit court in the county where you live or where the respondent lives

coalition_name: Violence Free Minnesota
criminal_definition: Stalking is engaging in conduct the actor knows or has reason to know would cause the victim to feel frightened, threatened, oppressed, persecuted, or intimidated, and that actually causes that reaction, including following or monitoring in person or by technological means and repeated unwanted calls, texts, or electronic messages.
criminal_penalty: Gross misdemeanor, up to 364 days in jail or a fine of up to $3,000; aggravated violations: felony, up to 5 years or $10,000; pattern of stalking conduct: felony, up to 10 years or $20,000.
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was found; § 609.749 expressly covers following, monitoring, calls, texts, and electronic messages.
order_duration: Up to 2 years; up to 50 years for repeat harassment
order_free_note: Filing fees are waived if the petition alleges acts that would violate Minn. Stat. § 609.749, subd. 2, 3, 4, or 5, or §§ 609.342 to 609.3451.
order_where: District court in the county where either party resides or in the county where the alleged harassment occurred

coalition_name: Mississippi Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposefully engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person, or making a credible threat, knowing or having reason to know it would cause a reasonable person to fear for their own safety, another person's safety, or damage to property.
criminal_penalty: Stalking: up to 1 year in county jail or a fine of up to $1,000, or both (up to a $1,500 fine if a protective order was in effect); aggravated stalking: felony, up to 5 years and $3,000, or up to 6 years and $4,000 if the offender is a registered sex offender and the victim is under 18.
cyber_note: Cyberstalking is a felony covering electronic threats and repeated electronic communications intended to threaten, terrify, or harass.
order_duration: Temporary order: up to 30 days, or up to 1 year if the parties have no minor children together; final order: as long as the judge believes is necessary.
order_free_note: There is no fee to get or serve a protection order.
order_gap_note: Mississippi has no separate civil stalking order — stalking victims use the Domestic Abuse Protection Order.
order_where: Municipal, justice, county, or chancery court

coalition_name: Missouri Coalition Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposely, through a course of conduct, disturbing or following another person with the intent to disturb them, where the conduct has no legitimate purpose and would cause a reasonable person to be frightened, intimidated, or emotionally distressed.
criminal_penalty: First-degree stalking: class E felony, up to 4 years in prison and a fine of up to $10,000; second-degree stalking: class A misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail and a fine of up to $2,000 (class E felony for repeat offenses or an officer victim).
criminal_statute: Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 565.225 (stalking, first degree) and 565.227 (stalking, second degree)
cyber_note: Missouri has no separate statute named cyberstalking; the harassment statutes cover any act, including electronic communications, done with the purpose of causing emotional distress.
order_duration: Full order: 180 days to 1 year; 2 to 10 years if the judge finds the respondent poses a serious danger.
order_free_note: There is no filing fee or court costs associated with filing orders of protection.
order_statute: Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 455.010-455.085 (Adult Abuse Act); petition under § 455.020
order_where: Circuit Court in the county where the petitioner resides

coalition_name: Montana Coalition Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposely or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct (two or more acts) directed at a specific person, knowing or having reason to know it would cause a reasonable person to fear for safety or suffer substantial emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: First offense: up to 1 year in county jail or a fine of up to $1,000, or both; second or subsequent offense within 20 years, or a first offense involving a protection-order violation, force or a weapon, or a minor victim with an offender at least 5 years older: up to 5 years in state prison or a fine of up to $10,000, or both.
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was found; § 45-5-220 expressly includes following, monitoring, and communicating by electronic devices or means, including GPS.
order_duration: Temporary order: up to 20 days; final order: for a period set by the court or permanently.
order_free_note: It does not cost anything to get or serve an order of protection (Mont. Code Ann. § 40-15-204(8)).
order_where: District court, city court, or justice court

coalition_name: Nebraska Coalition to End Sexual and Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is willfully harassing another person, or a family or household member of that person, with the intent to injure, terrify, threaten, or intimidate them.
criminal_penalty: Class IIIA felony under § 28-311.04.
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was found; 'course of conduct' under § 28-311.02 includes telephoning, contacting, or otherwise communicating with the person, including by electronic means.
order_duration: 1 year
order_free_note: Fees to cover filing, issuance, or service of a harassment protection order shall not be charged, except if the court finds by clear and convincing evidence the petition was false and sought in bad faith.
order_where: File the petition with the clerk of the district court; the case may be heard by the county court or the district court

coalition_name: Nevada Coalition to End Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is willfully or maliciously engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, or harassed and that actually causes the victim to feel that way.
criminal_penalty: First offense: misdemeanor, up to 6 months in jail or a fine of up to $1,000; second offense: gross misdemeanor; third or later offense: category C felony, 1 to 5 years; aggravated stalking: category B felony, 2 to 15 years and a fine of up to $5,000.
cyber_note: Nevada has no statute using the word 'cyberstalking'; § 200.575(4) makes stalking a category C felony when electronic means are used to publish, display, or distribute information in a way that substantially increases the risk of harm or violence to the victim.
order_duration: Temporary order: up to 45 days; extended order: up to 2 years.
order_free_note: There is no filing fee to obtain a protection order.
order_name: Order for Protection Against Stalking and Harassment
order_where: Any court of competent jurisdiction; in practice, the justice court

coalition_name: New Hampshire Coalition Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposely, knowingly, or recklessly engaging in a course of conduct targeted at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for personal safety or the safety of an immediate family member, and that actually places the person in such fear.
criminal_penalty: Class A misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail or a fine of up to $2,000; second or subsequent offense within 7 years: class B felony, 3 1/2 to 7 years in prison or a fine of up to $4,000.
order_duration: Up to 1 year, extendable for 1 year on a showing of good cause and thereafter for up to 5 years per extension.
order_free_note: There is no fee to file.
order_where: District (circuit) court in the district where the plaintiff or defendant resides

coalition_name: New Jersey Coalition to End Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposefully or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct directed at or toward a person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for their own safety or the safety of a third person, or to suffer other emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: Crime of the fourth degree, up to 18 months in prison and a fine of up to $10,000; crime of the third degree (up to 5 years, up to $15,000) if committed in violation of a court order, as a second or subsequent offense against the same victim, or while incarcerated or on parole or probation.
cyber_note: Cyber-harassment is a crime of the fourth degree for making online communications through any electronic device or social networking site with the purpose to harass, including threats to inflict injury or harm.
order_duration: Temporary order: until the final-order hearing, generally within 10 days; final protective order: no expiration date, until a court dissolves it.
order_name: Temporary Protective Order (and Final Protective Order) under the Victim's Assistance and Survivor Protection Act (VASPA)
order_where: Superior Court, Family Division, in your county

coalition_name: New Mexico Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Knowingly pursuing a pattern of conduct that would cause a reasonable person to feel frightened, intimidated, or threatened, intending to place the victim in reasonable apprehension of death, bodily harm, sexual assault, confinement, or restraint, or to cause fear for the victim's or a household member's safety.
criminal_penalty: Stalking: misdemeanor, up to 364 days in jail and/or up to $1,000 fine; second or subsequent conviction: fourth-degree felony; aggravated stalking (NMSA 1978, § 30-3A-3.1): fourth-degree felony, second conviction third-degree felony.
cyber_note: Harassment includes a pattern of conduct with an electronic communication device intended to seriously alarm or terrorize, and stalking under § 30-3A-3 includes remote surveillance by an electronic communication device.
order_duration: For a fixed period of any length the court finds appropriate to protect the victim; the order may be extended.
order_free_note: No filing, issuance, or service fees are charged for a petition for an order of protection.
order_where: District Court in the county where the victim resides; stalking is defined as domestic abuse under the Act whether or not the stalker is a household member

coalition_name: New York State Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Intentionally and repeatedly following, monitoring (in person or electronically), or engaging in a course of conduct toward another person, knowing or having reason to know it is likely to cause fear of material harm to physical, mental, or emotional health, or fear of suicide or self-inflicted injury.
criminal_penalty: Stalking in the fourth degree: Class B misdemeanor; third degree: Class A misdemeanor; second degree: Class E felony, up to 4 years in prison; first degree: Class D felony, up to 7 years in prison.
cyber_note: New York has no separate cyberstalking statute; stalking under Penal Law § 120.45 expressly includes following or monitoring by electronic means.
order_duration: Up to 8 years from sentencing for a felony conviction, 5 years for a Class A misdemeanor, and 2 years for any other offense.
order_gap_note: New York has no standalone civil stalking order a victim files on their own — protection comes through the criminal case: the order is issued by the criminal court handling the stalking case or at sentencing.
order_name: Order of Protection under Criminal Procedure Law § 530.13
order_where: The criminal court handling the stalking case (Criminal Court, Supreme Court, or local court where the criminal action is pending); New York has no standalone civil stalking order a victim files on their own — protection comes through the criminal case

coalition_name: North Carolina Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Willfully and repeatedly harassing another person, or engaging in a course of conduct without legal purpose, knowing or having reason to know it would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety or suffer substantial emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: First offense: Class A1 misdemeanor, up to 150 days in jail; repeat offense: Class F felony; stalking while a court order prohibiting the conduct is in effect: Class H felony.
cyber_note: Cyberstalking covers using email or other electronic communication to threaten bodily harm or property damage, or to repeatedly communicate to abuse, annoy, threaten, terrify, or harass; a Class 2 misdemeanor.
order_duration: A permanent order lasts for a fixed period of up to one year.
order_free_note: No court costs or fees are charged for filing or serving the complaint and orders under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 50C-2.
order_where: District Court, filed through the Clerk of Superior Court in the county where the case is filed

coalition_name: CAWS North Dakota (North Dakota Council on Abused Women's Services)
criminal_definition: Intentionally engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that frightens, intimidates, or harasses them and serves no legitimate purpose, or unauthorized tracking of a person's movements or location by GPS or other electronic means.
criminal_penalty: Class A misdemeanor (up to 360 days in jail, up to $3,000 fine); Class C felony (up to 5 years in prison, up to $10,000 fine) if the offender has a prior conviction for certain offenses against the victim or the stalking violates a court protection order.
cyber_note: Stalking includes unauthorized tracking of a person's movements or location by GPS or other electronic means, and harassment under N.D.C.C. § 12.1-17-07 covers threats and repeated contact by electronic communication.
order_duration: Up to two years.
order_where: District Court in the county where the victim lives

coalition_name: Ohio Domestic Violence Network
criminal_definition: Engaging in a pattern of conduct (two or more actions or incidents closely related in time) that knowingly causes another person to believe the offender will cause physical harm to them or a family or household member, or cause mental distress.
criminal_penalty: First offense: first-degree misdemeanor, up to 180 days in jail and/or up to $1,000 fine; fourth-degree felony (6 to 18 months in prison, up to $5,000 fine) if the offender has a prior menacing-by-stalking conviction or another aggravating factor applies.
order_duration: Up to five years.
order_where: Court of Common Pleas in the county where the victim lives

coalition_name: Oklahoma Coalition Against Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: Willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly following or harassing another person in a manner that would cause a reasonable person (or a member of their immediate family) to feel frightened, intimidated, threatened, harassed, or molested, and that actually causes the victim to feel that way.
criminal_penalty: First offense: misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail and/or up to $1,000 fine; stalking while a protective order is in effect or a repeat offense: felony, up to 5 years; a second act of stalking within 10 years of a prior stalking conviction: felony, up to 20 years and/or up to $25,000 fine.
order_duration: Up to five years; a continuous order is possible in certain cases, such as a prior felony stalking conviction or a history of violating court orders.
order_free_note: No filing fee, service fee, attorney fee, or other fee or cost is charged to the victim for filing a petition for a protective order.
order_where: District Court in the county where the victim resides, the defendant resides, or the violence occurred

coalition_name: Oregon Coalition Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Knowingly alarming or coercing another person or a member of their immediate family or household by engaging in repeated and unwanted contact, where it is objectively reasonable for the victim to be alarmed or coerced and the contact causes the victim reasonable apprehension for their personal safety.
criminal_penalty: Class A misdemeanor (up to 364 days in jail); Class B felony if the person has a prior stalking conviction, is subject to an active protection order, or at least one instance of unwanted contact was a felony, unlawful dissemination of an intimate image, or unlawful use of a GPS device.
cyber_note: Oregon has no separate cyberstalking charge; online and electronic communications can qualify as stalking under ORS 163.732.
order_duration: Unlimited duration unless limited by law or court order.
order_where: Circuit Court — file a civil petition directly with the court, or start the process by filing a complaint with a law enforcement officer, who issues a citation ordering the respondent to appear in court within three judicial days

coalition_name: Pennsylvania Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Engaging in a course of conduct or repeatedly committing acts toward another person, including following without proper authority, or repeatedly communicating with another person, under circumstances showing an intent to place that person in reasonable fear of bodily injury or to cause substantial emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: First offense: misdemeanor of the first degree; second or subsequent offense, or a first offense after a prior conviction for a crime of violence against the same victim or family or household member: felony of the third degree.
order_duration: Up to 36 months (3 years).
order_free_note: There is no cost to file for a protection order.
order_gap_note: Pennsylvania has no general civil stalking order for adult victims — the Protection From Sexual Violence (SVP) order covers stalking only if it involved a sexual offense, and the Protection From Intimidation (PFI) order covers only a minor victim stalked or harassed by an adult. An adult stalking victim with no sexual offense has no ch. 62A order available.
order_name: Protection From Sexual Violence (SVP) order (only if the stalking involved a sexual offense) or Protection From Intimidation (PFI) order (only for a minor victim stalked or harassed by an adult); Pennsylvania has no general civil stalking order for adult victims
order_where: Court of Common Pleas at the county courthouse where the victim lives

coalition_name: Rhode Island Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly following or harassing another person with the intent to place that person in reasonable fear of bodily injury, or harassing another person.
criminal_penalty: Felony, up to 5 years in prison and/or up to $10,000 fine.
cyber_note: Cyberstalking and cyberharassment covers transmitting communications by computer or other electronic device for the sole purpose of harassing a person or their family; first offense is a misdemeanor (up to 1 year, up to $500 fine), and a second or subsequent conviction is a felony (up to 2 years, up to $6,000 fine).
order_duration: A final order lasts for a fixed period of up to three years and may be extended.
order_where: District Court in the county where the victim lives; a temporary order can be issued the same day the complaint is filed

coalition_name: South Carolina Coalition Against Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: A pattern of words or conduct, whether verbal, written, or electronic, that serves no legitimate purpose and is intended to cause, and does cause, a targeted person (and would cause a reasonable person) to fear death, assault, bodily injury, criminal sexual contact, kidnapping, or property damage to the person or a family member.
criminal_penalty: Felony: first offense up to 5 years in prison and/or up to $5,000 fine; up to 10 years and/or up to $7,000 fine if a restraining order or injunction was in effect; up to 15 years and/or up to $10,000 fine with a prior harassment or stalking conviction within 10 years.
cyber_note: Stalking expressly includes a pattern of words or conduct, whether verbal, written, or electronic, that causes reasonable fear of harm.
order_duration: A fixed period of not less than one year, as determined by the court; the order may be extended for good cause.
order_free_note: A $55 filing fee is assessed to the non-prevailing party.
order_where: Magistrates Court in the county where the defendant resides, where the harassment or stalking occurred, or where the plaintiff resides if the defendant is a nonresident or cannot be found

coalition_name: South Dakota Network Against Family Violence and Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: Stalking is willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly following or harassing another person, making a credible threat intended to place the person in reasonable fear of death or great bodily injury, or repeatedly harassing another person by verbal, electronic, digital media, mechanical, telegraphic, or written communication.
criminal_penalty: Class 1 misdemeanor for a first offense; a second or subsequent conviction within 10 years, or stalking while a protection order is in effect, is a Class 6 felony.
cyber_note: The stalking statute itself covers repeated harassment by means of verbal, electronic, digital media, mechanical, telegraphic, or written communication, so online harassment can be charged as stalking.
order_duration: Up to five years
order_free_note: There are no costs or fees associated with obtaining or serving a Stalking Protection Order.
order_where: File a petition with the clerk of the circuit court; magistrate courts share jurisdiction over stalking protection orders.

coalition_name: Tennessee Coalition to End Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is a willful course of conduct involving repeated or continuing harassment of another person that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, threatened, harassed, or molested, and that actually causes the victim to feel that way.
criminal_penalty: Stalking is a Class A misdemeanor (up to 11 months, 29 days in jail, fine up to $2,500); aggravated stalking is a Class E felony (1 to 6 years, fine up to $3,000); especially aggravated stalking is a Class C felony (3 to 15 years, fine up to $10,000).
cyber_note: Tennessee has no separate cyberstalking statute; the stalking definition expressly includes unconsented contact by electronic communication such as email, text messages, and social media messages.
order_duration: Up to one year
order_free_note: No filing fee is charged for an order of protection for domestic abuse, stalking, or sexual assault.
order_where: File a sworn petition in circuit, chancery, or general sessions court in the county where you live, where the respondent lives, or where the abuse occurred.

coalition_name: Texas Council on Family Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is knowingly engaging, on more than one occasion and as part of the same scheme or course of conduct directed at a specific person, in conduct that constitutes harassment or involves threats of bodily injury, death, or property damage, which the actor knows or reasonably should know the other person will regard as threatening.
criminal_penalty: Third-degree felony (2 to 10 years in prison, fine up to $10,000); a second or subsequent stalking conviction is a second-degree felony (2 to 20 years, fine up to $10,000).
cyber_note: Texas has no separate cyberstalking statute; online conduct is prosecuted under the stalking statute, Tex. Penal Code § 42.072, which covers electronic conduct.
order_duration: For the duration of the lives of the offender and victim, or for a shorter period stated in the order; if no period is stated, the order lasts until the second anniversary of the date it was issued.
order_name: Protective Order for Victims of Stalking (Chapter 7B)
order_where: File an application for a protective order under Chapter 7B in the court in the county where you live; no relationship to the offender is required.

coalition_name: Utah Domestic Violence Coalition
criminal_definition: Stalking is intentionally or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that the actor knows or should know would cause a reasonable person to fear for their own safety or the safety of another, or to suffer other emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: Class A misdemeanor for a first offense; third-degree felony if the actor has a prior stalking conviction or violated a permanent criminal stalking injunction; second-degree felony if a dangerous weapon was used or the actor has two or more prior stalking convictions.
cyber_note: The stalking statute expressly includes using a computer, the Internet, text messaging, or any other electronic means as part of the course of conduct.
order_duration: Three years from the date the ex parte civil stalking injunction is served
order_where: File a verified written petition in the district court in the judicial district where you or the respondent resides or is temporarily domiciled, or where any of the events occurred.

coalition_name: Vermont Network Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposefully engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that the person knows or should know would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety or the safety of a family member, or to suffer substantial emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: Up to 2 years in prison, a fine up to $5,000, or both; aggravated stalking under 13 V.S.A. § 1063 carries up to 5 years in prison, a fine up to $25,000, or both.
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was verified from an official source; the stalking definition in 12 V.S.A. § 5131 covers use of an electronic, digital, or geolocation device to surveil a specific person.
order_duration: For a fixed period set by the court, extendable on the plaintiff's motion for such additional time as the court deems necessary to protect the plaintiff
order_free_note: No filing fee is required for an order against stalking or sexual assault.
order_where: File a complaint with the Civil Division of the Superior Court; available only against someone who is not a family or household member.

coalition_name: Virginia Sexual and Domestic Violence Action Alliance
criminal_definition: Stalking is engaging in conduct on more than one occasion with the intent to place another person in reasonable fear of death, criminal sexual assault, or bodily injury to that person or to a family or household member.
criminal_penalty: Class 1 misdemeanor (up to 12 months in jail, fine up to $2,500); a second or subsequent conviction within 5 years is a Class 6 felony (up to 5 years in prison, fine up to $2,500).
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was verified from an official source.
order_duration: Up to two years, extendable for additional periods of up to two years each on the petitioner's motion
order_free_note: There is no charge to file or serve a protective order petition in Virginia.
order_where: File a petition in General District Court; non-family abuse protective orders cover stalking, threats, or acts of violence by someone who is not a family or household member.

coalition_name: Washington State Coalition Against Domestic Violence & Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: Stalking is intentionally and repeatedly harassing or following another person, or knowingly installing or monitoring an electronic tracking device without consent to track another person's location, in a way that would cause a reasonable person to feel frightened, intimidated, or harassed.
criminal_penalty: Gross misdemeanor (up to 364 days in jail, fine up to $5,000); Class B felony (up to 10 years in prison, fine up to $20,000) if aggravating factors apply, such as a prior harassment or stalking conviction, violation of a protective order, or use of a deadly weapon.
cyber_note: Cyber harassment is making an electronic communication with intent to harass, intimidate, or torment another person; it is a gross misdemeanor, or a Class C felony if aggravating factors apply.
order_duration: One year from the date of the order, unless a different end date is listed in the order
order_free_note: An antiharassment protection order carries a filing fee (about $53), waived if the conduct includes stalking, a hate crime, violence, or a threat of violence, or if the petitioner cannot pay.
order_where: File a petition in district court or superior court in the county where you live.

coalition_name: West Virginia Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is engaging in a course of conduct directed at another person with the intent to cause that person to fear for their personal safety, the safety of others, or to suffer substantial emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: Misdemeanor: fine up to $1,000, up to 6 months in jail, or both; a second or subsequent conviction is a felony (1 to 5 years in a state correctional facility, fine $3,000 to $10,000).
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was verified from an official source.
order_duration: Up to two years
order_free_note: No filing fee is charged for a personal safety order petition under W. Va. Code § 53-8-13.
order_where: File a petition with the magistrate court in the county where you live, where the respondent lives, or where the abuse occurred.

coalition_name: End Domestic Abuse Wisconsin
criminal_definition: Stalking is intentionally engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person under the same circumstances to suffer serious emotional distress or to fear bodily injury to or the death of themselves or a member of their family or household.
criminal_penalty: Class I felony (up to 3.5 years in prison, fine up to $10,000); Class H felony (up to 6 years) with prior convictions; Class F felony (up to 12.5 years, fine up to $25,000) in the most serious cases.
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was verified from an official source; the course of conduct in Wis. Stat. § 940.32 includes electronic contact such as text messages and social media.
order_duration: Not more than four years
order_free_note: A filing fee applies, but it can be waived under Wis. Stat. § 814.61(1)(e) for petitioners who cannot pay.
order_where: File a petition with the clerk of the circuit court in the county where you live; no domestic relationship with the respondent is required.

coalition_name: Wyoming Coalition Against Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: Stalking is engaging, with intent to harass another person, in a course of conduct reasonably likely to harass that person, including communicating with, following, or placing the person under surveillance by electronic, digital, or GPS means.
criminal_penalty: Misdemeanor: up to 1 year in jail, fine up to $750, or both; felony stalking (prior conviction, serious bodily harm, violation of a protection order, or other statutory triggers): up to 10 years in prison.
cyber_note: The stalking statute expressly covers using any electronic, digital, or global positioning system device to communicate with, follow, or surveil the victim.
order_duration: Up to three years, extendable for additional periods of up to one year each
order_free_note: There is no fee to file the petition or to have it served.
order_where: File a petition in the circuit court in the county where you live, where the stalker lives or is found, or where the stalking occurred; no special relationship with the stalker is required.
